metadata.title: The Detector Was Never the Standard
metadata.purpose: deep-explainer: five linked mechanisms showing how AI similarity detection replaced a doctoral integrity standard it was never designed to be

beats.new_visual_element: ClaudeComposerAsk cold open — ask types, answer resolves
beats.narration_text: This is Liam, in for Bear. The answer on screen is no — and not because nobody looked. The text the 2015 case left behind was readable by the instrument that found it. Text produced in 2026 is not. What this episode examines: what the detector was actually measuring, what the rule it came to stand for actually says, and why those two things stopped being the same one.

props.command: A 2015 PhD thesis reused 322 sentences from someone else's. If it had been written in 2026, would anyone have found out?

beats.new_visual_element: Watermark mechanism: statistical bias → word selection → z-score → p-value
beats.narration_text: Then watermarking. A statistical bias is introduced when each word is chosen — a thumb on the scale. Count how many words landed on the marked side. Compute a z-score. Elegant, and honest about what it measures.
